title: Volkswagen Nears Deal to Sell Stake in India Unit to JSW Group
excerpt: The German automaker is in advanced talks with Sajjan Jindal's conglomerate to bring in a local equity partner for Skoda Auto Volkswagen India, with a potential agreement expected within weeks.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Volkswagen is in advanced talks with JSW Group for a stake in Skoda Auto Volkswagen India.
  • JSW aims for a majority stake, but key investment details remain unresolved.
  • Volkswagen holds only 2.5% of India's passenger vehicle market, below its 5% target by 2030.
  • Volkswagen AG is in advanced negotiations with JSW Group for a strategic investment in its Indian subsidiary, Skoda Auto Volkswagen India Pvt. Ltd.
  • JSW is reportedly seeking a majority stake, though valuation, investment size, and capital commitments remain unresolved.
  • The deal would end VW's years-long search for a domestic partner as it aims to grow beyond its current 2.5% share of India's passenger vehicle market.

Volkswagen AG is closing in on a deal to sell a stake in its Indian subsidiary to Sajjan Jindal-led JSW Group, according to a Bloomberg News report published Tuesday. The German carmaker and JSW are working toward a potential agreement in the coming weeks that would see the Indian conglomerate invest in privately held Skoda Auto Volkswagen India Pvt. Ltd., according to people familiar with the matter.

The move, if finalised, would mark the most significant restructuring of Volkswagen's India operations since the company entered the market more than two decades ago.

What's on the Table

Senior executives from both companies have recently held meetings, but several key issues remain unresolved, according to Bloomberg. These include the valuation of the business, the size of JSW's proposed investment, and future capital commitments from both sides.

JSW is reportedly seeking a majority stake in the venture, though the discussions remain fluid and could still fall apart. The talks are confidential, and neither party has publicly confirmed the negotiations.

"Volkswagen is constantly evaluating new business opportunities and various business options to implement its strategy in India."

— Volkswagen spokesperson, responding to Bloomberg

A Volkswagen spokesperson added that "India is an important market for Skoda Auto's global growth plans" but declined to comment specifically on the JSW discussions.

Why Volkswagen Needs a Partner

Despite investing over $2 billion in India across more than 20 years, Volkswagen has struggled to gain traction in the country's cost-sensitive passenger vehicle market. The Volkswagen Group—which includes Skoda, Audi, Porsche, Bentley, and Lamborghini—currently holds about 2.5% of India's passenger vehicle market, well below its stated target of 5% by the end of the decade, according to Bloomberg.

The company had previously pursued a partnership with Mahindra & Mahindra, but those talks collapsed due to divergent strategic priorities and valuation disagreements, according to Autocar India. The JSW Group subsequently emerged as the preferred partner.

Volkswagen's Indian subsidiary had also abandoned the costly MQB A0 37 platform in favour of the more versatile CMP21 architecture, projected to support internal combustion, hybrid, and electric SUVs. But the project's estimated investment exceeds €1 billion, and VW Group has made clear that a local equity partner is needed to share the financial burden and secure project approval.

JSW's Auto Ambitions

For JSW Group, the deal would deepen its growing footprint in India's automotive sector. The Jindal-led conglomerate already holds a 35% equity stake in JSW-MG Motor India, a joint venture with China's SAIC Motor. JSW has also signed an agreement with the Odisha government to establish an integrated EV and battery manufacturing plant in Cuttack and Paradip with an anticipated investment of ₹40,000 crore.

Discussions between JSW and Volkswagen reportedly began around three years ago and initially centred on the possible use of VW's manufacturing facilities in Pune and Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar. More recently, negotiations broadened to include an equity investment, according to Bloomberg.

"Partnerships remain a strategic option to combine cultural alignment with business goals. The train has not left the station yet."

— Klaus Zellmer, Global CEO of Skoda Auto, at the Munich Mobility Show

What a Deal Could Mean for the Indian Auto Market

A successful tie-up would give JSW access to Volkswagen's global vehicle platforms and could create opportunities for collaboration beyond India. For Volkswagen, it would reduce funding requirements at a time when the company is pursuing wider cost-cutting measures across its global operations. Bloomberg reported that VW had already scaled back its planned investment in a new India-focused electric vehicle platform to around $700 million from an earlier $1 billion.

India's passenger vehicle market—now the third largest globally—has become an increasingly attractive destination for international automakers seeking local partnerships. The Skoda-VW and JSW discussions underscore how global carmakers are leaning on domestic partners to absorb risks, navigate regulatory complexity, and capture growth in the market.

What's Next

Both sides are reportedly working toward a deal in the coming weeks. However, the discussions could still collapse, and no formal agreement has been reached. A mid-2027 launch for vehicles on the CMP21 platform remains the internal target, but that timeline depends on the partnership being finalised and investment greenlit.

For the Indian diaspora, the potential deal signals deeper global-Indian industrial integration in one of the world's most consequential auto markets—and could influence the trajectory of EV manufacturing in India for years to come.
